title: Sprocket & Sprout
pitch: Take over an old keeper's clockwork farm and bring it back machine by machine, until it runs itself like a music box.
number: 2.1 "Overseas": a merchant ship buys your exports
about: You arrive in the valley town of Thistlewick to take over the old keeper's clockwork farm. The works stand rusted around one preserving crock still bubbling on its last beans. Bring them back machine by machine: within minutes an arm you restored is carrying pickles to the shipping crate, a gleaner picks the field you planted, and the keeper's water wheel turns the grist mill by the river.

Every machine tells you what it is doing and why it stopped, so a stuck line is a puzzle you can solve instead of a mystery. The town is your customer: fill its orders, rank up with each business, and bring back the mill, the waterworks, the street lamps, the tram and the clock.
Hand farming is still here whenever you want it, and the morning summary names yesterday's biggest bottleneck.

2.1, "Overseas", opens the Harbor: late in the game a merchant ship, the Copper Gull, calls at the beach pier with a manifest from a port across the sea, asking for goods in amounts only a factory can make, like 300 iron bars or 2,000 glass. Fill it and climb six ranks, from Dockhand to Merchant Prince.
madeWith: TypeScript and Canvas, no engine. Code written with Claude Opus from my design docs; pixel art made with PixelLab; sound made procedurally.
platforms: Browser (installable as an app), Windows installer

title: Overgrowth
pitch: Raid the jungle by day and carry home what you can. Hold the Heartwood by night. Survive ten nights and find out what happened to the 1931 expedition.
about: By day you hack through the jungle with a machete, forage the forest floor, and search old camps, wrecks, temples and root caches for what's inside. Everything you carry weighs something, so you choose what to bring home before dusk. At camp you craft it into towers, barricades and traps at the Workbench, Fire Pit and Tinker's Bench, and build them around the Heartwood, the glowing shrine at your camp.

At dusk the Blight crawls out of rifts in the forest and looks for the side your towers cover least. The Heartwood can only feed so many roots, so every defence is a budget call, and each kind of Blight shrugs off some damage types and breaks under others. Hold until dawn. Each night is harder, every fifth night brings a boss, and the Rot Mother comes on night 10. Endless mode keeps going after that.

1.0, "The Lost Expedition", turned the day into a scavenging run and added a story: twelve torn pages from a 1931 expedition, three seals that put rifts to sleep, grafts for your towers, a radio that calls supply drops, and two endings. It also added key rebinding, captions, colour-blind outlines, partial gamepad support, twenty achievements and a daily vigil.

1.1, "New Growth", rebuilt the trees and remodelled the Wisp, Husk and Rot Mother while drawing about a third of the triangles. 1.2, "Hold Fast", fixed everything a full playthrough review found: the machete now answers every click, giants have buttresses and strangler figs, Continue picks up at the hour you left, and six bow towers can no longer hold night 10 alone. 1.2.1 replaced the droning night music with cues and silence.
madeWith: JavaScript moving to TypeScript, and Three.js. Code written with Claude; surfaces and foliage generated with Flux, the hero models built in Blender from Python scripts, and the sound synthesized live.
platforms: Browser (desktop, keyboard and mouse; partial gamepad)

title: Arcwarm
pitch: A Quake Live lightning-gun duel against a bot, with Halo gravity and shields. The duel is the warm-up.
about: A 2–5 minute aim warm-up you play as a game. You and a bot share the same movement and the same lightning gun, so you track while you move and dodge, and the bot's beam punishes predictable movement.

Halo gravity and air control, Quake Live gun and hitbox numbers. Lifesteal is on by default: every hit heals the shooter, so a fight is decided by who misses more. The bot's aim comes from perception delay and your movement, not dice, across five levels from Easy to Nightmare.
Two maps: Pinehollow, a forest bowl with a treehouse, a shrine and a man cannon, and the White Room, a plain grid with ramps.
madeWith: JavaScript and Three.js. Code written with Claude Opus from my design notes.

title: Verdant Relay
pitch: Scavenge by day. Hold the line by night. Loot an overgrown city, then defend the Relay with what you brought home.
number: 4 nights · loot only counts if you get home
about: You are a scavenger supplying Verdant Relay, a power-and-comms hub built into an overgrown transit station. By day you head into the jungle with a machete: finish the day's quest, grab loot and blueprints, then get home before sunset. Loot only counts if you get home, and after dark it's worth 1.5 times as much, if you dare to stay out.

By night you defend the Relay with towers on glowing pads, and you're on the board yourself: swing, roll, deflect and hold E at a tower to overcharge it. A run is 4 nights, and the Canopy Colossus attacks on the last one. Research from every run buys permanent unlocks, and feats open four scavengers and eight legendary relics.

The signal update gave the game an ending: kill the five area bosses across your runs, build the Uplink, and hold its signal through the Colossus. It also made runs shorter, the first run simpler, and cut a lot of reading.
madeWith: JavaScript moving to TypeScript, and Three.js, rendered as pixel art. Code written with Claude Opus from my design docs; every sprite drawn pixel by pixel by Claude in build scripts.

title: Fins & Fronds
pitch: Scape, stock and care for every real kind of aquarium, from Iwagumi stone gardens to Malawi rockwork and reefs, and grow a little fish shop into a grand oceanarium.
about: You get the keys to an empty fish shop. Set up tanks, landscape them with sand, stone, driftwood and plants, and stock them with fish, shrimp, snails and corals. Keep the water right: the game tracks real water chemistry, from the nitrogen cycle to pH, hardness and salinity.

Build a real kind of tank and the game recognizes it, from a community tank to Rio Negro blackwater or a Lake Malawi rock shore, then rates it on wellbeing, habitat, scape, authenticity and spectacle. Visitors pay to see it, though you never see them, only their nose prints on the glass.

Breed stock to sell, send expeditions to 27 regions for new species, and grow from a Little Fish Shop to a Grand Oceanarium with reefs, kelp towers, jellyfish, rays and big sharks. Version 0.3 added an ending, letters that write back and leave keepsakes, a week with a market day and a school trip, and conservation projects. Name your favorite animals (named ones are never sold), and press V to watch any tank full screen.
controls: Switch tanks / back to the hall
madeWith: TypeScript and one HTML canvas, no engine. Code written with Claude Opus from my design docs and aquarium research; pixel art from PixelLab, and the sound synthesized.

title: Pixel RTS
pitch: Mine ore, pump oil, build armies and capture cities. Win by conquest, by science, or by holding the map. Up to six players online, nothing to install.
about: A top-down pixel-art RTS inspired by The Conquerors 3 and Strategema on Roblox. Start with an HQ, mine ore and pump oil, build barracks, factories, airfields and docks, capture and grow cities, and research a tech tree across four eras.

Play a skirmish against up to five AIs with four personalities, or play online with friends: the host's browser runs the game and friends join with a room code, peer to peer, with no game server. Land, air and sea units, with a destroyer, battleship and submarine triangle at sea. On Pangaea and Lakes maps, a river splits the players into two sides, crossed by two stone bridges. Each player can build 21 buildings plus 4 for every city they hold, and you can sell units back for half their cost. Two mega units, the Mega Tank and the Mega Plane, top the tech tree, and the Launch Site's rocket counts down on everyone's screen. Six-player presets set up a 3 v 3 or a six-way free-for-all, and a sandbox mode hands everyone unlimited cash, oil and science.

It has twists of its own: a government in exile, a last stand at the HQ, insurgency for knocked-out players, city contract auctions and bounties, coalitions and wanted aces. New players get First Orders, a guide that points at the very next click for the first six steps of any match, or can start with Boot Camp.
madeWith: TypeScript and Canvas 2D, no engine; online play is peer to peer over WebRTC. Code written with Claude Opus from my design docs; pixel art from PixelLab.

title: Foldworks
pitch: Build a production line, fold it into a single tile, and build the next, bigger floor out of what you folded. For a frog mayor who really wants Gizmos.
number: 70 s audit → grade S+ to D → one tile
about: Start on a floating island with a hand furnace and a pile of iron ore you mine by clicking. Build lines on a grid with miners, belts, smelters, presses and assemblers, and sell what reaches the Dock to Mayor Bramble, a frog who really wants Gizmos.

The twist is folding. When a line runs well, draw a box around it: a 70-second audit measures what goes in and out and grades it from S+ to D, and the whole line becomes one tile that keeps producing at that rate. Stamp copies, then build the Factory floor out of your folded modules.

Every machine says what it's waiting for, so a jam is a puzzle, not a mystery. Five acts take you from the Workshop to the Factory, the District, the World and Beyond, with three resets you choose (Reorganize, Relocate and the Last Fold). The Playability Update makes folding the second research, so your first fold comes in about 5 minutes, ends the story at the Floating City with credits, and opens Challenges and Scenarios after it.
madeWith: TypeScript and one HTML canvas, no engine. Code written with Claude Opus from my design docs; pixel art from PixelLab plus pieces Claude draws pixel by pixel in scripts, and the sound made procedurally.

title: Stillframe
session: 40 short levels, saves in your browser
pitch: Time moves when you move. Stand still and the world crawls; walk and it runs. Red glass enemies shatter in one hit, and so do you.
about: A top-down pixel-art take on SUPERHOT. Stand still and the world crawls at 3% speed, walk and it runs, and every shot or throw buys a split second of full-speed time. Grab guns, punch, throw whatever is in your hands, and clear each room of red glass enemies that shatter in one hit, just like you.

Five chapters, 40 levels: office floors, the subway and its trains, rooftops with ledges and a crane, a nightclub that strobes on the beat, and a white void where the rules glitch, each ending in a boss. Every level has 3 stars and a par time, and every clear plays back as a replay.
Coins for clean, stylish play buy Workshop upgrades that bend the time rule: walk cheaper, dash in zero time, rewind a death. After the story, the Gauntlet sends endless waves through five arenas.
madeWith: TypeScript and Canvas 2D, no engine. Code written with Claude Opus from my design docs; pixel art from PixelLab plus sprites Claude draws pixel by pixel in scripts, and the sound synthesized.

title: Deepwick
pitch: You wake in a meadow with nothing. Punch a tree, build a shelter before the first night, then dig down through a mountain full of tunnels to whatever is drinking the light.
about: No pick, no lantern, no food. Just a valley of trees, a mountain full of tunnels, and the old mining town of Deepwick long gone quiet. Punch a tree, build a workbench, and make a pick, a shelter, a door and a bed before the first night falls, because when the sun sets the Hollows climb out. They burn at dawn.

Then go down. Smelt ore, forge better tools at the anvil, cook at the fire, and find the heart crystals and relics buried in the dark, from the Topsoil Tunnels through the Mossroot Grotto, the Crystal Hollows and the Ember Depths to the Sunless Vault. Somewhere under all of it, the Gloamheart is beating.

Build deeds and settlers come: Pell to trade, Brannoc to sharpen your steel, Wren to read the relics. The latest update was a survival overhaul: you start with nothing, there's a day and night cycle, hunger and farming, a 40-slot pack and a wider world with natural cave mouths.
controls: Lamp oil / tonic / recall to bed
madeWith: TypeScript and Canvas 2D, no engine. Code written with Claude Opus; pixel art from PixelLab, packed into sprite sheets by script.

title: Aldervale
pitch: Farm for the castle on the hill. Grow the crops, mill the flour, bake the bread, and fill the royal requisitions to turn a little plot into the finest farm in the valley.
number: 3 crops to start · requisitions pinned to the board
about: High on the western hill stands Aldervale Castle, and its kitchens are always hungry. You're the steward of a small homestead below it. Hoe the plots, sow wheat, tomatoes and pumpkins, water them, and carry the harvest in your basket.

The castle's requests are pinned to the board: the Royal Kitchens, Head Cook Marigold and the Steward of Aldervale each want something. Fill a requisition and Pip the courier takes it up the hill for coin and Royal Favour.
Favour and coin go back into the farm: production buildings that mill and bake, and new fields to expand into. It's an early build with a first loop to try.
madeWith: TypeScript and Three.js. Code written with Claude Opus; every model built in Blender from Python scripts, and the textures generated by script.

title: Dumpster Alchemy
pitch: Run the night shift at a raccoon-run landfill. Merge junk into better junk, keep the stink down, and build the Trash King.
about: Drag junk onto matching junk to merge it up the chain, and feed the raccoons' orders before the stink builds up. Junk left sitting goes smelly, so keep it moving and hit the night's quota before 6 AM.

Drop different junk together to brew one of 20 recipes: a boot and a tire make a Monster Truck Shoe. Tools like Electric Soup and the Junk Magnet help, cascades and the Stench Streak build up to a Raccoon Rave where everything pays triple.

Version 2.0, "The County Run", makes a run 10 nights across Lot 9, the Marina and Mount Trashmore, with a map where every road forks, rule-bending Contraband and three boss nights. Or play the Daily Dump.
madeWith: TypeScript and Canvas 2D, no engine. Code written with Claude Opus; pixel art drafted with PixelLab and finished by script, and every sound synthesized.
platforms: Browser (mouse or touch; phones in landscape)

title: The Mountain Is a Machine
session: Long sessions, 3 save slots in your browser
pitch: Run a company dig site at the foot of a mountain that hums. Build belts and machines, fix a giant drill and bore down through six layers to find what's making the noise.
about: You run a company dig site at the foot of Old Thrum. Lay belts, place miners and machines, repair a giant broken drill, and bore down through six layers: the Surface, the Shallows, the Fungal Caverns, the Crystal Depths, the Magma Shelf and the Alien Strata.

Each layer is its own factory floor, linked to the others by freight elevators, with one strange material and one hazard that you learn to turn into a tool. The Company sends contracts, sells licenses and runs the power line; the Field Manual covers the basics.
Version 0.2, "Build it yourself", starts a new game with only the HQ, a Terminal and a Drill, and walks you through building the first line step by step, with a hint and a map marker for each step.
madeWith: TypeScript, no engine. Code written with Claude Opus; pixel art from PixelLab, built into one atlas by script.

title: Goblin Pension Plan
session: Two chapters, saves in your browser
pitch: A low-ranking goblin turns a soggy alcove under the city into a home before the Adventurers' Guild clears it out. Scavenge, fight, sneak and do the paperwork.
number: 2 chapters · a pension box with 6 rungs
about: You're a low-ranking goblin living in a soggy maintenance alcove under the city of Bellmarket. This morning the Adventurers' Guild put your home on its survey list. Only a chartered burrow is off the Guild's books, and charters come from the Goblin Cooperative, with paperwork.
Scavenge the tunnels, fight with a Scrap Launcher, sneak past adventurers or throw a pebble to send them looking somewhere else, and craft your way to a Burrow that gets cozier as you go.

Chapter Two is the Pension Plan: work orders from Grubb's in-tray, permits for Proper Walls, Indoor Plumbing and a Four-Poster, each one changing how the Burrow looks and sounds, all the way to Retirement Day. A playability pass also made the first trip fairer and added a guide line that names your next step.
madeWith: TypeScript and Canvas 2D, no engine. Code written with Claude Opus; most of the pixel art from PixelLab, with code-drawn art as the fallback.

title: Formica
pitch: Raise an ant colony from a single queen. Watch it dig, forage, fight and grow, then send out winged queens to found daughter colonies.
about: Release a queen on the ground and watch her dig her first chamber. Her workers tunnel out food stores, nurseries, granaries and middens, forage the surface, and age from nurse to builder to forager. You don't control the ants: you keep them, with sugar, mealworms, leaves over the entrance before rain, berry bushes, root aphids and a marker for where to dig.

Five real species play differently, from tireless black garden ants to carpenter ants, big-headed ants, fire ants that raft their queen out of a flood and honeypot ants that store honey in living workers. Pick a meadow, woodland floor, sandy dunes or riverbank, each with its own soil, weather and danger: antlion pits, centipedes, robins and a summer army-ant raid.

Survive a winter and the colony raises winged queens and males. After the nuptial flight you can follow a daughter queen to a new patch of ground, with traits she inherits from how her mother's colony lived. Version 1.2, "Wider World", added the biomes, pheromone trails, the lineage and the dangers.
controls: V Q W E U R I T Y
madeWith: TypeScript and Canvas 2D, no engine. Code written with Claude Opus from real ant biology; pixel art from PixelLab, and the sound synthesized.

title: Ember
pitch: Steer a glowing wisp through the void and evolve it. The void evolves too: it watches how you kill and grows an answer to it.
number: 5 sectors · the void answers how you kill
about: You're a wisp of light drifting through the dark. Move to steer, pulse to burst the void's creatures, close loops with your burning trail, and light FEVER when it's ready. Mutations grow you into a Wisp, then a Flame, and every apex you slay evolves you further.

The void learns. Kill with the pulse and it grows shells, kill with loops and it grows wards, and every answer it grows names its counter. Split your kills so no weapon makes 60% of them and the void can't read you. It remembers you between runs, and the title shows what it holds.

Fly through five sectors, from the Shallows to the Event Horizon, each with an apex boss at the end. Version 1.0, "The Void's Turn", added the void's answers, earned forms, a kill-cam and run history, and icons for every mutation.
madeWith: TypeScript and WebGL2, no engine. Code written with Claude Opus; mutation icons from PixelLab, the glow from a post-processing pipeline, and the music and sound synthesized.
platforms: Browser (mouse and keyboard; touch works too)

title: Last Watt
pitch: A tower defense where energy is a live flow. Your towers are lights, and they fire on watts, not ammo.
number: 12 kW Lamp → 6 kJ/s, if the grid can feed it
about: An enemy's health is in kJ, and a Lamp drawing 12 kW does 6 kJ/s only if the grid can feed it. Build more towers than your Burners can run and the whole wall slows down together. Keep the Hearth lit for 12 waves, then see how long it lasts in endless.

Four maps, six towers with branching upgrades, and seven enemies that each hit the grid a different way: Shades cut Nodes, Snuffers put out Burners, Siphons drink from your lines. Each Node carries at most 60 kW, so where the power goes is a decision.
This one is a work in progress, built to find out whether the idea is fun.
madeWith: TypeScript and Canvas, no engine. Code written with Claude Opus from my design docs; pixel art from PixelLab plus sprites Claude draws pixel by pixel in code.

title: Smeltdown
session: Two acts a run, saves between fights
pitch: A deckbuilder where your deck is the factory. Machine cards run themselves at the end of every turn and feed what they make into your next hand.
number: Ore → Ingot → Steel Blade in one end of turn
about: Machine cards build into your Factory and run at the end of every turn, left to right. Each one takes what the machines to its left just made, then what's in your hand: a Drill Rig digs Ore, a Smelter turns it into Ingots, an Assembler forges a Steel Blade, and it all lands in your next hand on top of your normal draw. Before you end the turn, every machine shows whether it will run and the tray shows what you'll get.

Machines make Heat. At 5 you're Hot and hit harder; at the top of the gauge you melt down. Enemies fight the factory too: they jam machines, steal from your tray and throw Rust, Burns and Slag into your deck.

Two acts on branching maps: 61 cards (22 of them machines), 15 enemies including 3 bosses, 27 Parts, shops, rest stops and 9 events. This one is a work in progress, built to find out whether the idea is fun.
madeWith: TypeScript and the DOM, no engine. Code written with Claude Opus from my design docs; pixel art from PixelLab plus icons and backdrops Claude draws pixel by pixel in scripts, and the sound synthesized.
